questions.question: Fill in the blank: All squares are ____.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: All ____ triangles are similar.

Isosceles triangles can have different angles.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks: Two polygons of the same number of sides are similar, if (a) their corresponding angles are ____ and (b) their corresponding sides are ____.
questions.explanation: Similar polygons have equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides.
option_feedback: Correct! Equal angles and sides in the same ratio.
It is the other way round: angles equal, sides proportional.
Equal sides would make them congruent; similar needs only proportional sides.
Corresponding angles must be equal, not supplementary.

questions.question: Give two different examples of a pair of (i) similar figures, (ii) non-similar figures.
answer_steps: (i) Similar: two circles of radii 2 cm and 5 cm; two equilateral triangles of sides 3 cm and 6 cm.
(ii) Non-similar: a square and a rectangle that is not a square; an equilateral triangle and a right triangle.

answer_steps: Produce $AD$ to $E$ so that $DE = AD$, and $PM$ to $L$ so that $ML = PM$. Join $CE$ and $RL$.

In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle PQR$: $\dfrac{AB}{PQ} = \dfrac{AC}{PR}$ and $\angle A = \angle P$, so $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQR$ (SAS).

questions.question: If $AP$ and $DQ$ are medians of triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$ respectively, where $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF$, then prove that $\dfrac{AB}{DE} = \dfrac{AP}{DQ}$.
answer_steps: $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF$ gives $\angle B = \angle E$ and $\dfrac{AB}{DE} = \dfrac{BC}{EF} = \dfrac{2BP}{2EQ} = \dfrac{BP}{EQ}$.

questions.question: In $\triangle ABC$, $D$ and $E$ are points on $AB$ and $AC$ such that $DE \parallel BC$. If $AD = x$, $DB = x - 2$, $AE = x + 2$ and $EC = x - 1$, find $x$.
$\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF$ with $AB = 3$ cm, $BC = 4$ cm and $CA = 5$ cm. If $DE = 6$ cm, find $EF$, $FD$ and the perimeter of $\triangle DEF$.
In $\triangle PQR$, $S$ and $T$ are points on $PQ$ and $PR$ such that $ST \parallel QR$. If $PS = 4$ cm, $SQ = 6$ cm and $ST = 3.2$ cm, find $QR$.
answer_steps: $ST \parallel QR$, so $\angle PST = \angle PQR$ and $\angle PTS = \angle PRQ$ (corresponding angles): $\triangle PST \sim \triangle PQR$ (AA).

questions.question: Prove that if a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio. Hence, in $\triangle PQR$, a line $\ell$ intersects the sides $PQ$ and $PR$ at $L$ and $M$ respectively such that $LM \parallel QR$. If $PL = 5.7$ cm, $PQ = 15.2$ cm and $MR = 5.5$ cm, find the length of $PM$ (in cm).
answer_steps: Given $\triangle ABC$ with $DE \parallel BC$, $D$ on $AB$, $E$ on $AC$. To prove $\dfrac{AD}{DB} = \dfrac{AE}{EC}$. Join $BE$, $CD$; draw $DM \perp AC$ and $EN \perp AB$.
$\text{ar}(BDE) = \text{ar}(DEC)$ (same base $DE$, between the same parallels), so $\dfrac{AD}{DB} = \dfrac{AE}{EC}$.

questions.question: State and prove the Basic Proportionality Theorem. Using it, find $AE$ if in $\triangle ABC$, $DE \parallel BC$, $\dfrac{AD}{DB} = \dfrac{2}{3}$ and $AC = 18$ cm.
answer_steps: Statement: if a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.
Proof: join $BE$ and $CD$, draw $EN \perp AB$ and $DM \perp AC$; then $\dfrac{\text{ar}(ADE)}{\text{ar}(BDE)} = \dfrac{AD}{DB}$ and $\dfrac{\text{ar}(ADE)}{\text{ar}(DEC)} = \dfrac{AE}{EC}$.

questions.question:
At 4 pm, a student 1.2 m tall casts a shadow 0.9 m long, while the school flagpole casts a shadow 6 m long.

(i) Which criterion shows that the two triangles are similar? (1)

(ii) Find the height of the flagpole. (1)

(iii) At the same time, a building casts a shadow 15 m long. Find its height. OR How long is the shadow of a 4 m tall tree at that time? (2)
answer_steps: (i) AA: both have a right angle, and the sun's rays make the same angle with the ground.

questions.question:
A roof frame is a triangle $ABC$ with a horizontal beam $DE$ parallel to the base $BC$, where $D$ is on $AB$ and $E$ is on $AC$. $AB = 6$ m, $AD = 2$ m and $BC = 9$ m.

(i) Why is $\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC$? (1)

(ii) Find the length of the beam $DE$. (1)

(iii) If $AE = 2.5$ m, find $AC$. OR If $AE = 2.5$ m, find $EC$. (2)
answer_steps: (i) $DE \parallel BC$, so $\angle ADE = \angle ABC$ and $\angle AED = \angle ACB$ (corresponding angles): AA.
